minutes.headline: Assessors push GIS vendor for a fee schedule while racing to fix lakefront neighborhoods by December bills
minutes.summary:
The Board of Assessors met mainly to prepare for redoing property "neighborhoods" townwide under a state DOR directive, starting with long-disputed lakefront classifications, and to review what their GIS vendor (heard as CI/CGI) already provides versus what costs extra. No major votes were taken beyond routine signing of excise commitments and a motion to adjourn into executive session over abatement/exemption matters.</parameter>

what_happened.line: A consultant aims to reclassify the disputed lakefront neighborhood in time for the December tax bill, though called an aggressive, non-guaranteed target.
The board asked its GIS vendor for an updated written fee schedule ahead of a May 12 vendor meeting.
The board signed routine motor vehicle, trailer, and boat excise commitments without a formal vote.
The finance director will check whether supplemental tax bills have gone out and report back next meeting.
The board voted to adjourn into executive session to discuss abatement and exemption matters.

why_it_matters: Homeowners in the lake-area neighborhood could see their property classification, and with it their assessment, change as soon as the December tax bill.
The GIS vendor's fee schedule will determine what the town pays for the mapping tools used to draw and redraw assessment neighborhoods townwide.
Residents waiting on a supplemental tax bill will learn its status once the finance director reports back.
watch_next: May 12 GIS vendor meeting, where the written fee schedule is expected
December tax bill, the target for the lakefront neighborhood reclassification
